angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 5,389,588 km at 116.55 pc = 0.62 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17608: distance 116.55 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.043), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 116.55 +/- 5.012 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 7.0670 +/- 0.2862 mas (same row, RUWE 2.33), 24.7 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 7.747 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17608: radius 7.747 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 211.434 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.783) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 5,389,588 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 7913 +/- 3358 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17608: effective temperature 7913 +/- 3358 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.448) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 17608: effective temperature 7913 +/- 3358 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.448) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * 23 Tau: main object type Be*, Be Star
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * 23 Tau: projected rotation speed 195 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2005yCat.3244....0G)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 215) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 2.92 from 2001A&A...378..861C; the 2 published values span log g 2.92 to 4, across which the limb law changes by at most 2.6% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2001A%26A...378..861C)
